scope: Instruction-memory-connected integer/branch/jump execution subset. Predecoded TAGE/RAS/JALR-target prediction (TAGE=0 selects gshare) with checkpoint repair (rtl/frontend/branch_predictor.sv), held line traffic and branch recovery, full-window external restart. No CSR/trap service, load/store execution, cache, architectural-suite acceptance of this top or clock claim. This acceptance profile pins FRONTEND_FAULTS=0; the enabled fault-insertion profile is checked separately. This historical profile pins TRAP_SERVICE=0; architectural trap acceptance is checked separately.
faults: Frontend fault tokens and unsupported instructions stall fetch-to-dispatch. Backend target-alignment faults remain held raw ROB-head candidates. None is converted into a finalized trap event; they require future precise fault insertion/head control. Younger fetch faults may be discarded by older branch recovery. unsupported_o marks raw unsupported valid lanes, including a tail ignored behind lane-zero CFI.
recovery: Only branch resolution competes internally. resolve_grant_i gives the caller permission to defer it; accepted branch recovery always has frontend redirect capacity. External flush_i wins and supplies flush_pc_i, restores committed rename state and preserves retirement order. The caller chooses a restart PC consistent with committed state. No multi-event arbiter is claimed.
flow: Frontend take is exactly backend allocation acceptance. TAGE=1 (default) selects the 512-byte TAGE direction tables; TAGE=0 retains gshare. Conditional history is speculative at accepted dispatch and trains at ordered retirement using next PC differs from PC+4. TAGE carries 36-bit recovery checkpoints; gshare carries 12. JAL uses its encoded target, returns the RAS and other JALR the retired target table. A predicted-taken lane ends the offered group. See verif/frontend/README.md for retirement re-lookup, dual-update ordering and repair semantics. enable_i controls new fetch demand. Sticky instruction-protocol fatal disables dispatch, issue, completion, resolution and retirement until reset.
drain: The core recycles ROB identities itself. On identity_drain_o it stops new fetch demand, waits until the window is empty, no instruction transaction is offered or outstanding, no producer, system or memory work is held and flush_ready_o is high, restart-flushes to the committed next PC (last retired or trap pc_after, else the last external flush PC or reset PC), then pulses the internal drain. identity_drain_o falls when the recycle completes. External drained_i remains legal under the same conditions with enable_i low; generations never silently wrap.
